The identical file shipped by the Linux, macOS and WebAssembly variants of this package is attested as a byte-for-byte duplicate in noticesAlreadyCovered.

id: VLC plugins built under the GPL (bundled by VideoLAN.LibVLC.Windows)
licenseText:
NOTE: Section 1 lists VideoLAN.LibVLC.Windows as LGPL-2.1-or-later, and that is correct for libvlc and libvlccore themselves - but it is NOT the licence of every binary the package carries. The package ships 323 plugin modules for win-x64, and two of the ones this application depends on are built under the GPL rather than the LGPL: libavcodec_plugin.dll and libswscale_plugin.dll, which wrap FFmpeg libraries configured with --enable-gpl (the build stamp is present in both binaries). They are required, not incidental: removing them was tested and breaks HEVC and MPEG-4/AVI playback, because the remaining decoders fall back to Windows Media Foundation, which does not cover those formats here. Both plugins are statically linked (--enable-static --disable-shared), so code from several further libraries is compiled INTO libavcodec_plugin.dll rather than loaded from separate DLLs, and ships with it: LAME 3.100 (LGPL - build flag --enable-libmp3lame, with LAME's own version stamp, project URL http://lame.sf.net and runtime strings present in the binary), OpenJPEG (BSD-2-Clause, --enable-libopenjpeg) and libgsm (permissive, Technische Universitaet Berlin, --enable-libgsm). Their full licence texts are not reproduced here; they travel with the corresponding source named below, which is the route by which they are supplied. Note that LAME is LGPL and statically linked, so the relink provision of LGPL section 6 is satisfied through that source route rather than by replacing a file - unlike the LGPL libraries this application ships as separate assemblies. The other GPL modules in the package are NOT shipped - plugins/codec/libx26410b_plugin.dll (an H.264 encoder), plugins/lua/liblua_plugin.dll, plugins/audio_filter/libdolby_surround_decoder_plugin.dll and plugins/audio_filter/libheadphone_channel_mixer_plugin.dll are excluded in DiffusionNexus.UI.csproj, as is the whole lua/** tree (95 files of VLC web-interface assets, 16 of them GPL-2.0-or-later, which nothing can load once the Lua plugin is gone), as are the win-x86 and win-arm64 payloads in their entirety. The GPL set was determined from the binaries themselves rather than from package metadata, and DiffusionNexus.Tests/Licensing/VlcPayloadLicenseTests.cs re-derives it on every test run so that a VLC version bump introducing a new GPL module fails the build instead of shipping unattributed. These plugins are separate files under libvlc/win-x64/plugins/, loaded at runtime by libvlc; they are not linked into the application executable, and this application is itself MIT-licensed, which is GPL-compatible. CORRESPONDING SOURCE: it accompanies this distribution, in the source/ folder beside the application. GPL-2.0 section 3 offers three ways to supply source - accompany the binary with it, make a written offer valid three years, or pass along an offer received - and this release takes the first, which is why no offer is made here and no contact address is given: there is nothing to request. source/ contains the unmodified upstream archives for VLC 3.0.23 (the binaries identify themselves as 3.0.23 'Vetinari', git revision 3.0.23-2-0-g79128878dd, read from libvlc.dll's version resource rather than inferred from the NuGet package number 3.0.23.1), FFmpeg at the exact commit VLC pins for this release, and LAME, OpenJPEG and libgsm at the versions VLC's contrib build pins for it. Each is listed with its SHA-256 and origin in source/README.txt. None of that is the source of this application, which is MIT-licensed and published at https://github.com/Little-God1983/DiffusionNexus. The staging is performed by Scripts/Fetch-CorrespondingSource.ps1, which verifies every archive against its pin and aborts the release rather than shipping source that does not correspond to the shipped binaries.
